Motorcycle Accidents Can Inflict Catastrophic Injuries

Motorcyclists are at a higher risk of serious and fatal injuries in traffic accidents than typical motor vehicle drivers. Per vehicle mile traveled in 2019, motorcyclists were 29 times more likely than passenger vehicle drivers to pass away in accidents and 4 times more likely to be injured,
according to the NHTSA
. A motorcycle accident can inflict serious injuries on an unprotected motorcyclist, including:
Broken bones
Soft-tissue injuries
Deep lacerations
Burns
Road rash and traumatic tattooing
Internal damage
Facial and dental injuries
Head trauma/skull fractures
Traumatic brain injuries
Back, neck and spine injuries
Permanent paralysis
Scarring and disfigurement
Long-term disabilities
Death

Common Causes of Motorcycle Accidents in Thornton

Liability, or financial responsibility, for a motorcycle accident, will go to the at-fault party in Colorado under the state’s tort-based insurance system. Before an insurance company will offer a settlement, however, the injured victim must prove fault using a preponderance of the evidence. This is evidence that the defendant is more likely to be at fault than not at fault. The liable party may be the other driver for a careless or reckless act, such as:
Distracted driving.

If a driver is paying less than 100 percent attention to the road, he or she can easily miss a motorcycle and cause an accident. The most common form of distracted driving is texting and driving or cell phone use.
Speeding.
Speeding is one of the most common causes of serious and fatal car accidents in Colorado. A speeding driver may be unable to hit the brakes in time to avoid colliding with a motorcyclist.
Right-of-way violations.
Motorcyclists are owed all of the same rights as other motorists. This means that drivers must yield them the right-of-way at intersections, when applicable.
Following too closely.

Following too closely, also known as tailgating, can be deadly for a motorcyclist if it causes a severe rear-end collision. Motor vehicle drivers should always maintain a safe distance between their cars and nearby motorcycles.
Weaving between traffic.
Drivers must signal their intent to change lanes or pass and only do so when they can safely. Weaving or drifting between lanes or unsafe passing can cause a motorcycle accident.
Driving under the influence.

Driving while impaired by drugs or alcohol is against the law in all 50 states. Drunk drivers often make reckless decisions and have delayed reaction times that increase the risk of motorcycle accidents.

Driving while tired. Drowsy driving can be just as dangerous as drunk driving. If a driver falls asleep behind the wheel, he or she may crash into a motorcyclist without hitting the brakes – causing a serious high-speed collision.

However, it could be the manufacturer of your motorcycle for a defective part, the government in charge of roadway maintenance or a third party. Identifying multiple parties can lead to greater financial compensation available. Determining liability and proving fault may take assistance from an experienced motorcycle accident lawyer in Thornton.
Who Is Liable for My Injuries?

Colorado is a fault car insurance state. This means that after a motorcycle accident, you will file a claim with the insurance company of the at-fault driver or party. Determining liability for your collision is one of the first steps you must take to recover from a motorcycle accident.

A lawyer can investigate your crash to determine fault and search for evidence of liability, such as proof that the driver wasn’t paying attention to the road or was in violation of a traffic law at the time of the crash. The most common party liable for a motorcycle accident in Thornton is a negligent driver. However, a third party could also be liable, depending on the facts of the case.

If your motorcycle had a defective part that caused a dangerous equipment breakdown, for example, the manufacturer of the part could be liable. Another common scenario is the city or state being held liable for a motorcycle crash caused by a road defect, such as a pothole or obscured traffic sign.
What if I Am Partially Responsible for the Accident?

Don’t assume that you are ineligible for financial compensation if you are partially responsible for a motorcycle accident. Thanks to Colorado’s comparative negligence law, you may still be entitled to at least partial compensation. As long as you are found to be less than 50 percent responsible for the crash, you can still collect compensation from the other at-fault driver or party.

If you are allocated a percentage of fault, however, your settlement or judgment award will be reduced by an equivalent amount. For example, if you are awarded $100,000 in damages for your medical bills and motorcycle repairs but are given 10 percent of the blame, your award will be reduced to $90,000. If you are found to be 50 percent or more at fault for the crash, your recovery will be reduced to $0. This is why it is important to have an attorney defend your rights if you contributed to your motorcycle accident.
What Damages Could I Recover for a Motorcycle Accident in Thornton?

“Damages” is legalese for the financial compensation that is available in a civil lawsuit. If it is determined that your motorcycle accident claim against a driver or another party is valid, that party’s insurance company will be responsible for paying for your related economic and noneconomic losses.
Economic losses can include:
Medical bills (including future necessary medical care)
Treatment and rehabilitation costs
Losses of income
Lost future capacity to earn due to a disability
Travel or transportation costs
Childcare costs
Attorney’s fees and other out-of-pocket expenses
Noneconomic damages include:
Physical pain and suffering
Emotional trauma and distress
Mental anguish
Post-traumatic stress disorder
Depression or anxiety
Inconvenience
Lost enjoyment of life
Loss of consortium
Long-term disability or disfigurement
If your loved one passed away in a fatal motorcycle accident in Thornton, your family may also be entitled to
wrongful death damages

. These can pay for the reasonable costs associated with your loved one’s funeral and burial, as well as lost earnings and inheritance. Discuss the value of your motorcycle accident case with one of our lawyers for more information before accepting an insurance settlement.
Motorcycle Accident Laws in Thornton, Colorado

Motorcyclists are subject to all of the same laws and responsibilities as other motorists in Colorado. For example, they have a right to take up a full lane on the road and are not allowed to lane split, or ride on the line between two lanes. They must obey all of the same traffic signs and control signals as other drivers, including speed limits and stop lights.

In addition to traditional traffic laws, motorcyclists are also subject to special rules reserved for them. Motorcyclists under the age of 18 must wear helmets. All riders and passengers, regardless of age, must also wear eye protection. In addition, motorcyclists in Colorado must have a special motorcycle endorsement on their drivers’ licenses to operate this type of vehicle.

Motorcyclists should only carry passengers if their motorcycles were designed for passengers, with a designated seat and footrests. If a motorcyclist breaks any of these state laws, he or she can be held partially or wholly responsible for a related accident. The same is true if a driver violates a traffic law and causes a collision.
Time Limit to File a Motorcycle Accident Claim
Don’t wait if you believe you have grounds for a motorcycle accident claim in Thornton. Colorado law places a
three-year

deadline on your right to file a lawsuit, in most cases. While the general statute of limitations is two years for a personal injury case, this deadline is extended by one year (for three years total) if the case involves a motor vehicle accident.

For the most part, there are no exceptions to the statute of limitations; if you wait too long to file and miss your deadline, you will be barred from making a financial recovery. This is why you should contact an attorney right away.
